Purpose This document defines the **visual taste and world logic of Odaiba 2127**. It exists to prevent the project from drifting into: - renovated 2027 architecture, - generic premium smart-city design, - generic sci-fi, - cyberpunk, - contemporary glass-and-steel architecture with futuristic props added afterward, - or unrelated futuristic objects that do not belong to the same city. Every new object and every evolution of an existing building must feel as if it belongs to **one continuous 100-year urban lineage**. The key question is not: > “Does this look futuristic?” The key question is: > **“Could this only belong to Odaiba 2127?”** --- # 1. Visual source of truth The reference set contains six views of the **same city**. They are not six alternative concepts. They are six views used to understand different aspects of one world. ## Reference hierarchy ### R01 — MASTER HERO **Highest visual authority.** Defines: - overall future intensity, - district-scale architectural DNA, - city density, - megaframe language, - circular / spherical lineage, - aerial mobility presence, - material tone, - relationship with Tokyo Bay, - atmosphere, - and the overall visual threshold for “2127”. World premise Odaiba 2127 is not a preserved 2027 district with futuristic additions. Over one century, the architectural ideas of the original Fuji TV building have evolved into the **operating system of an entire waterfront district**. The original Fuji TV building is therefore treated as **genetic origin**, not as an object that must be copied. Its deeper architectural DNA is: - exposed structural frame, - object suspended inside frame, - circle / sphere, - square grid, - diagonal circulation, - large voids, - elevated connections, - visible infrastructure, - civic monumentality. By 2127 these ideas have expanded into: - district-scale urban chassis, - suspended civic ecosystems, - hybrid public infrastructure, - three-dimensional mobility networks, - ring and circular interchange systems, - adaptive waterfront architecture, - ecological infrastructure, - public spaces distributed across multiple vertical levels. The desired result should feel like: > **Fuji TV → architectural DNA → district-wide urban evolution** not: > Fuji TV → futuristic renovation. --- # 3. Core design principle ## RADICAL SYSTEMS, RESTRAINED AESTHETICS The future should come from **changed urban systems**, not decorative sci-fi styling. The city can be radically different in: - structure, - movement, - ecology, - waterfront logic, - public-space organization, - building typology, - media systems, - logistics, - energy and climate response. But the aesthetic remains controlled. Avoid: - excessive neon, - cyberpunk color, - arbitrary glowing objects, - random flying vehicles, - sculptural sci-fi blobs, - visual clutter, - fantasy anti-gravity forms. The future is radical because the **city operates differently**, not because every surface is visually loud. --- # 4. The 2127 test Every major design must pass this question: > **If the futuristic vehicles and lighting were removed, would the architecture and urban system still be impossible to mistake for 2027?** If the answer is **no**, the design is not futuristic enough. A successful design should remain recognizably 2127 in clear daylight. --- # 5. Replace typologies — do not decorate them Do not futurize the appearance of 2027 urban typologies. Replace the typologies themselves. ### Avoid - conventional road - ordinary car street - bus stop - monorail station - office tower - shopping mall - glass business campus - slab + cylindrical column system - planter tree - rooftop garden - conventional ferry pier - escalator bank - skybridge between two towers ### Prefer - post-road civic terrain - three-dimensional mobility field - magnetic structural transit - multimodal civic interchange - inhabited megaframe - hybrid civic volume - suspended public ecosystem - branching / transfer structural systems - climate ecology - ecological infrastructure - amphibious mobility node - diagonal inhabited circulation - continuous elevated civic network The difference must be structural and spatial, not cosmetic. --- # 6. Architectural DNA Every building does **not** need to look the same. Every building does need to feel genetically related. Use the DNA through **rules**, not repetition. ## 6.1 Frame The frame may become: - urban chassis, - deep structural truss, - inhabited structural member, - mobility-support framework, - transfer structure, - large-scale public skeleton, - suspended infrastructure carrier. Avoid repeating simple white rectangular frames without functional purpose. ## 6.2 Circle / sphere Do not place identical silver spheres everywhere. The circular lineage may evolve into: - partial spheres, - hollow rings, - circular voids, - sliced spherical chambers, - ring transit nodes, - botanical climate chambers, - civic media chambers, - structural transfer rings, - circular water basins, - observation environments. Use circular geometry as a **family of typologies**, not a logo. ## 6.3 Diagonal movement Diagonal movement is one of the strongest pieces of Fuji-derived DNA. It may appear as: - inhabited slopes, - diagonal magnetic mobility, - ramps large enough to become public space, - inclined gardens, - diagonal civic streets, - suspended routes, - transfer systems crossing multiple levels. Avoid using ordinary escalators as the main expression. ## 6.4 Void Large voids are essential. The district should not become visually solid. Use voids to: - frame sky, - expose Tokyo Bay, - allow aerial routes, - create civic scale, - separate suspended volumes, - reveal multiple city layers, - maintain openness. --- # 7. Density rule ## MORE LAYERED, NOT MORE CROWDED Odaiba must retain: - open sky, - long sightlines, - visible water, - large negative spaces, - generous separation between major structures, - major structural voids. Future intensity should come from: - vertical layering, - suspended spaces, - mobility systems, - ecological layers, - elevated decks, - amphibious waterfront systems. Do not solve futurism by filling the skyline with towers. --- # 8. Building evolution rules When evolving an existing Odaiba building: ## Keep - useful spatial memory, - landmark relationship, - site role, - important urban alignment, - meaningful architectural DNA. ## Transform - building typology, - circulation, - structural logic, - public interface, - mobility integration, - ecological role, - envelope behavior, - vertical relationship with the district. Do not simply: - enlarge the old building, - add a glass shell, - add a rooftop garden, - attach flying-car docks, - add LED screens, - wrap it with futuristic bridges.
